- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.7) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often lags; shift forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in bullish sentiment periods; apply +1–2% bias to forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 cycles, model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast with sentiment direction for 2–3 days before reversing.
